newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU asks tourism head to take early retirement.
newsitem.headline: EU asks tourism head to take early retirement.

text.p: - The European Commission said on Thursday it had asked the German head of its tourism division, which has been rocked by accusations of mismanagement, to take early retirement.
But the Commission said it was still not ready to lift the diplomatic immunity of Director-General Heinrich Von Moltke, as requested by Belgian authorities.

"The grounds given for lifting the immunity weren't clear and were certainly not convincing enough in order for the Commission to take that decision," Commission spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas told a news briefing.
Von Moltke's division has been in the spotlight since Belgian officials last January arrested two officials in connection with an investigation of bribery and fraud.

Van der Pas said the move to replace Von Moltke was not linked to those two cases, however, and was not a reflection on Von Moltke's character. He said the Commission simply wanted to make some internal reforms.
"The Commission stresses the confidence it has in the integrity and the honourability of Mr Von Moltke," he said.

The European Parliament's budget committee last week threatened to freeze more than a quarter of the budget for European commissioners' salaries to force them to restructure the deparment to keep it scandal free.
But van der Pas said the Commission had already been planning to make changes at the department.

The two tourism officials were arrested after investigators discovered evidence that recipients of European Union subsidies to promote tourism had paid hundreds of thousands of dollars in "illegal commissions", a Belgian anti-fraud unit said.
Those two officials were fired by the Commission, van der Pas said.
Belgian authorities in June asked the Commission to lift the immunity of two other officials, including Von Moltke, and one former official in connection with the investigation.
